messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: Elevated TLS handshake errors from multiple customers to inference.redwood.com. Error rate spike on region eu-west-1 starting ~17:00 UTC. Pager: paged alex (oncall).

alex (oncall): saw it. getting eyes. grouping alerts now. errors ~502/ssl_handshake_failure and upstream connection reset.

ajdan (typo correction) -> alex (oncall): (ignore)

maya (infra): I'm pulling logs from the edge LB (alb-prod-1). can someone confirm if we rotated certs in the last deploy window?

infra-bot: deploy:cert-rotation pushed cert-inference-v3 to alb-prod-1 at 16:46 UTC by pipelines/auto.

alex (oncall): that's probably the only change in the 1h window. jordan, lee, can you join? I'll page ecs oncall if we need node-level traces.

jordan (sre): joining. initial metrics: TLS handshakes failed during ClientHello stage, clients see 'handshake_failure' and retries then 429s. Packet drops look networky in a quick tcpdump. posting snippet:```tcpdump -nni any 'tcp port 443' -c 20
17:02:03.123456 IP client > alb: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS,....], length 0
17:02:03.123457 IP alb > client: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 1, win 0, length 0
17:02:03.123458 IP client > alb: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,...], length 0
17:02:03.123459 IP alb > client: ICMP frag needed, mtu 1400
```

lee (neteng): ICMP frag needed suggests PMTU/MTU mismatch. any recent peering or MTU changes between VPCs?

maya (infra): We did a routing optimization last week for prod-peering, changed encapsulation to vxlan which implicitly set MTU to 1400 on peering interfaces on 2026-03-08. But that was green for 5 days.

alex (oncall): but infra-bot shows cert rotation at 16:46. Could a bigger cert chain push the ClientHello over MTU and trigger fragmentation issues?

jordan (sre): yes plausible. New cert chain adds ~1.2k bytes for a full chain + OCSP stapling, combined with TLS extensions (ALPN, SNI) can push a single ClientHello past PMTU. Some middleboxes drop fragments or block fragmented ClientHello.

lee (neteng): scanning peering logs: around 16:40 we saw a config push that lowered interface MTU on prod-peering to 1400 as part of vxlan rollout. before that it was 1500. That creates a 100-byte delta and if client MSS negotiation is not adjusted, first packet may be fragmented.

alex (oncall): customer-impact - Sam, can you pull which customers hit errors and if any critical jobs failed?

sam (customer-success): affected: 3 enterprise accounts (acme, libra-pay, edu-platform). acme reported errors in user-facing chat features, libra-pay saw transaction retries fail causing delays. I've opened CS tickets and sent an incident status email to account owners. they want ETA.

maya (infra): immediate mitigation options: 1) roll back cert-inference-v3 to v2 (smaller chain) on the ALB 2) increase MTU on peering to 1500 (risky, affects other tenants) 3) disable OCSP stapling temporarily to reduce response size 4) enforce TLS record splitting or reduce ALPN list (hard fast).

jordan (sre): can we test with a curl from within eu-west-1 to the ALB using the new cert to reproduce? alex, can you run:```curl -v --http2 https://inference.redwood.com/ -H 'Host: inference.redwood.com' --resolve 'inference.redwood.com:443:10.0.0.5'```

alex (oncall): running now from jump-euwest1... getting TLS handshake timeout, tcpdump below shows the SYN/ACK then immediate RST from ALB when ClientHello gets bigger.

alex (oncall): quick reproducer: I replaced the cert on a test ALB with v3 and hit it with `openssl s_client -connect alb-ip:443 -servername inference.redwood.com -tls1_2 -alpn h2` output:```CONNECTED(00000003)
139892...:error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number:../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:??
---
No client certificate CA names sent
Peer signing digest: SHA256
Server certificate
subject=/CN=inference.redwood.com
---
recv failed
```

lee (neteng): also saw ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed) from intermediate path. Suggests PMTU blackhole. Middleboxes may drop fragmented UDP/TCP TLS handshake fragments.

maya (infra): mitigation plan: 1) temporarily revert ALB cert to v2 for the prod host (low blast radius) 2) schedule peering MTU bump with neteng ASAP in a maintenance window 3) collect pcap from edge and path to provider for full RCA. Which should we do now?

alex (oncall): revert cert v3 -> v2 now if it's quick. I can trigger the rollback on alb-prod-1. jordan, can you watch logs while I swap?

jordan (sre): watching metrics. also enabling extra TLS debug logs for ALB and app proxy.

infra-bot: rollback initiated: cert-inference-v2 re-applied to alb-prod-1 by alex at 17:25 UTC.

alex (oncall): done. rolling health checks. initial handshake error rate dropping in 90s. 

sam (customer-success): telling customers: "We reverted a recently rotated certificate that exposed a path MTU issue causing TLS handshakes to fail. We are investigating and will follow up with RCA." they asked for ETA on a permanent fix.

lee (neteng): confirming: after rollback ICMP frag-needed messages stop and client handshakes succeed. That strongly points to cert size pushing ClientHello over PMTU and fragments being dropped.

jordan (sre): capturing full timeline: 16:40 MTU change on peering -> 16:46 cert v3 rotation -> 17:00 errors spike -> 17:25 cert rollback -> 17:30 error rate normalized. hypothesis: cert chain size + OCSP stapling caused ClientHello to exceed 1400 MTU -> fragmentation -> intermediate devices drop fragments -> handshake fails.

maya (infra): next steps for RCA: - collect pcaps from edge and intermediate path - get ALB config and cert chain sizes - check OCSP stapling size for v3 - verify which middleboxes (cloud provider transit) drop fragments - confirm if vxlan encapsulation caused effective PMTU drop - propose permanent fixes (regenerate cert chain with smaller chain, remove unnecessary intermediates, or ensure peering MTU 1500 and enable DF/PMTUD).

alex (oncall): immediate owner for follow-up: maya to lead infra RCA, lee to own peering/MTU, jordan to own detection/alerting (add alert for sudden ICMP frag-needed rates and handshake failures). sam will consolidate customer comms. I'll hand off oncall to jordan at 18:00 UTC - leave this thread open for final RCA notes.

jordan (sre): taking oncall at 18:00. noted. adding a runbook entry: if new cert rotation + MTU < 1500 then block rotation until PMTU verified.

sam (customer-success): customers acknowledged the rollback and are asking for timeline. I'll push estimated ETA for permanent fix (2 days) and offer a dedicated tech sync.

maya (infra): uploading logs to gcs and linking in ticket (internal). Will attach cert chain sizes and OCSP responses.

alex (oncall): status update to #general at 17:45: short blurb sent. thanks everyone for the quick triage. tagging this as "impact: partial, root-cause-proposed: cert chain size + peering MTU" in incident tracker.

lee (neteng): long term recommendation: enforce MTU gating in deploy pipeline (fail cert rotate if peering MTU < expected) and add synthetic tests that exercise large ClientHello.

jordan (sre): agreed. will draft post-incident checklist and include packet examples and timeline.

oncall-bot: reminder: please fill out post-incident form: /incidents/1755234000/form

alex (oncall): handing off. jordan now oncall. leaving notes in the tracker.

jordan (sre): wrapping up thread. collecting attachments and will start RCA doc tomorrow. please DM if you have raw pcaps or provider logs to add. :thumbsup:
